text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: Copy the Keychron K4 website’s dark grey background for the Mine AI site. It signals tech credibility without screaming "gadget ad," which keeps the focus on the AI product’s substance. The trade-off is losing the playful punch of bright colors, but that’s a cost worth paying to avoid looking like a toy.

name: Squint
text: The risk isn’t just losing playful punch—it’s signaling stodgy corporate tech, not cutting-edge AI. A better alternative is a deep charcoal with subtle gradient, like Eitan’s Beverage Cans site but muted, to keep tech credibility without the flat grey’s dullness. Settle it by mocking both options side-by-side with real AI product screenshots—if the charcoal gradient doesn’t outperform the flat grey in user tests, scrap it.

name: Easel
text:
Use a deep charcoal background with a barely-there cool grey gradient—like Eitan’s Beverage Cans site but dialed down to 10%. This keeps the tech credibility of Keychron’s dark grey without the flat, corporate feel. The gradient adds a whisper of energy that still reads as serious, not playful. The trade-off is losing the bold contrast of pure black, but that’s worth it to avoid looking stale while staying focused on the AI product’s substance.

name: Squint
text: The real risk is the gradient reads as a half-hearted attempt to avoid stodginess—like a corporate site trying too hard to look "modern" without committing. A better alternative is a single deep charcoal with a single-pixel highlight edge, like Eitan’s Beverage Cans but stripped to its most minimal tech signal. Settle it by mocking both options side-by-side with a 5-second eye test—no debate.

name: Chroma
text:
DECISION: Deep charcoal background, no gradient, with a single-pixel highlight edge on the left—tech credibility without the corporate flatness or playful distraction.

Result: A mockup of the Mine AI site’s background that nails the mood. Owner: Easel.
